context.description: Development of the Adaptive Navigation Engine
context.opening_question: What are we working on right now?

current_situation: All four regression tests pass with AI-generated proposals. The boundary between Engine interpretation and participant decision is now structurally enforced and observable. The tests do not depend on exact AI wording — only on structural properties. This means the Engine can change how it reasons without breaking the confirmed contract.

goals.desired_direction: Build the smallest executable loop that demonstrates Case File continuity, multiple goals with independent lifecycles, and Engine proposals that reflect accumulated observations. Use Python. Optimise for clarity and reversibility, not production architecture.

missions.name: Minimal Loop
missions.purpose: To establish the smallest executable demonstration of continuity, independent goal lifecycles, and observation-informed proposals before adding more sophisticated navigation logic.
missions.description: Create a small Python module that defines a CaseFile containing observations and multiple Goal records, each with its own status and history; implement an Engine step that accepts a participant update, appends an observation, evaluates each active goal independently, and returns a concrete proposal. Add a scripted run with at least two goals where one goal changes state while the other remains active, then add tests asserting that observations persist across steps and later proposals include relevant prior observations.
definition_of_done: The prototype runs from a clean Python environment with one documented command.
A CaseFile persists across at least two engine steps.
At least two goals exist and can transition independently without one goal's status changing the other.
Each engine step records an observation in the CaseFile.
A later proposal demonstrably changes or becomes more specific because of an earlier recorded observation.
The scripted run prints the current goals, accumulated observations, and the next proposal in a human-readable form.
Focused tests cover continuity, independent goal lifecycles, and observation-informed proposal generation.
missions.result: Implemented Case File, Goal, Mission, Observation, Decision dataclasses with JSON persistence. Created a rule-based Engine stub. Built a CLI loop and a non-interactive test.

missions.name: Add Reflection Rules
missions.purpose: To create the smallest concrete example of Engine behavior that reflects accumulated observations rather than merely carrying them forward.
missions.description: In the existing Python module, define two or three simple observation patterns such as progress, blockage, or uncertainty. For each active goal, inspect its accumulated observations and generate a goal-specific proposal: continue or increase difficulty after progress, suggest identifying a blocker after blockage, and request clarification after uncertainty. Add focused tests showing that a matching observation changes the relevant goal's proposal, an unrelated goal remains independent, and prior observations continue to appear in later decisions.
definition_of_done: A deterministic reflection rule is implemented in the Engine without changing the persistence model.
At least two observation signals produce visibly different proposals.
A proposal changes only for the goal whose observations support the change.
Tests demonstrate that relevant prior observations influence a later proposal.
The existing continuity, multiple-goal, and locally scoped GIVE UP behavior still passes.
The demonstration remains self-contained, readable, and reversible.
missions.result: Replaced the rule-based Engine reasoning with GPT-5.6 Luna. Ran the Skördefesten case as an A/B comparison against the v0.1 baseline.

missions.name: AI Regression
missions.purpose: Establish a small, repeatable behavioral contract for continuity, independent goal evaluation, accumulated-context use, and non-fabricating AI proposals.
missions.description: Create a Python test scenario with two active goals and two participant updates. Inject a deterministic AI response or model stub through the existing Engine boundary, run both steps, and assert that observations persist, each goal receives its own proposal, a progress or blockage update changes only the relevant goal's proposal, and no proposal claims an unobserved action was completed. Save one representative real-model response as a review fixture without making the test depend on live model availability.
definition_of_done: A two-goal, two-step scenario runs through the same Engine entry point used by the CLI.
The test confirms that both participant observations remain in the Case File after the second step.
The test confirms that an update relevant to one goal changes that goal's proposal while the unrelated goal remains independently represented.
The test confirms that the later proposal references or meaningfully uses prior observation context rather than merely returning a generic proposal.
The test rejects proposals that assert completion or observations not present in the Case File.
The deterministic regression test passes without network access.
A representative live AI output is recorded for manual comparison, without being treated as evidence of mission completion.
missions.result: Extracted scenario configuration from hardcoded Python into JSON files. Created a generic simulation runner with a three-layer model: scenario (starting conditions), simulation (repeatable participant responses), case file (accumulated state).

missions.name: Confirm Proposals
missions.purpose: To enforce the separation between what the Engine proposes and what the participant decides, making the core interaction principle visible and testable in the smallest executable loop.
missions.description: Add a pending proposal and participant-decision path to the Python simulation. Run a deterministic scenario where the Engine proposes a new goal, verify that the Case File goals remain unchanged before confirmation, then apply an ACCEPT decision and verify that the goal is added. Add a second path that rejects a proposal and verify that no goal is added. Preserve existing observation history and independent lifecycle behavior in both paths.
definition_of_done: The Engine can return a proposal without immediately creating or activating a Goal.
A deterministic test shows that an unconfirmed proposal leaves the Case File's goals unchanged.
An explicit ACCEPT decision adds the proposed goal with an identifiable initial status and history.
An explicit REJECT decision leaves the Case File's goals unchanged and records enough decision context to explain the outcome.
Existing observations and independent goal lifecycles remain intact after proposal and decision handling.
No test or output claims that a participant action occurred unless the scenario explicitly supplies that decision.
missions.result: Added an interpret-and-confirm step. The participant can now accept, correct, or reject the Engine's interpretation before a Goal is created. Tested with a correction that narrowed the direction from broad entrepreneurship to small practical income tasks.

missions.name: Test Correction Flow
missions.purpose: Ensure participant correction genuinely redirects future navigation and that the interpret-confirm boundary remains enforced.
missions.description: In Python, create a deterministic scenario with an existing active goal and a participant update that produces a pending interpretation. Apply a CORRECT decision containing narrower participant-supplied direction, assert that the original interpretation is not added as a goal, then run another Engine step. Assert that the new proposal reflects the corrected direction, the correction is preserved in Case File history, observations remain intact, and the unrelated goal receives no correction-derived change. Keep any model response supplied through the existing controllable adapter.
definition_of_done: A deterministic test exercises propose, correct, and subsequent Engine-step behavior.
The uncorrected interpretation does not create or alter a goal before participant confirmation.
The corrected direction is stored in the Case File and appears in the next relevant proposal.
Existing observations persist across the correction and later Engine step.
An unrelated active goal remains independent of the correction.
The test passes without requiring live model availability.
missions.result: Created a four-part regression test for the interpret-and-confirm boundary. Tests verify: correction changes goal direction, rejection leaves Case File unchanged, goal isolation holds, and continuity works after correction + mission + observation.

missions.name: Persistence Check
missions.purpose: Verify that Case File continuity and the Engine/participant decision boundary remain intact across save-and-reload, without coupling the test to exact AI wording.
missions.description: Create a deterministic two-goal scenario with at least two observations and a pending interpretation or correction. Save the Case File to JSON, load it into a fresh Case File and controllable Engine, continue with the next participant update and decision, and assert that observations, goal histories, pending state, and the resulting goal-specific proposals match the uninterrupted scenario.
definition_of_done: A test constructs a two-goal scenario, records observations, and creates a pending interpretation or correction.
The Case File is serialized and reconstructed through the existing JSON persistence path.
The reloaded case preserves observations, goal statuses, goal histories, and pending decision state.
Continuing after reload produces a proposal for each relevant active goal.
The proposal after reload reflects prior observations or confirmed correction data.
The unrelated goal remains unaffected by the correction or observation assigned to the other goal.
The test compares structural outcomes rather than exact model wording.
The uninterrupted and save-and-reload paths both avoid claiming completion of unobserved actions.

observations.text: The complete loop executes mechanically. Continuity works at the data level — the next proposal contains the previous observation text. Multiple goals coexist and GIVE UP is locally scoped. But the Engine adds no domain intelligence. All meaningful content came from the participant, not the Engine.

The AI Engine produced proposals that a participant could plausibly ACCEPT without modification. It used geographic and time context, generated specific missions with verifiable definitions of done, and built on previous observations with reasoning rather than verbatim quotation. The rule-based engine required MODIFY every time. The AI constraint held: it did not fabricate evidence or claim mission completion.

The same Engine handles radically different domains without code changes. The three-layer separation makes experiments reproducible. But the runner had a structural flaw: the Goal was created directly from the AI's interpretation without participant confirmation. This diverges from the documented principle that the Engine proposes and the user decides.

The correction fundamentally redirected subsequent proposals. Without it, the AI suggested startup thinking and investment strategies. With it, the AI focused on low-cost local services and practical demand testing. This confirms that the interpretation-confirmation step is not cosmetic — it changes the trajectory of the entire case.

All four regression tests pass with AI-generated proposals. The boundary between Engine interpretation and participant decision is now structurally enforced and observable. The tests do not depend on exact AI wording — only on structural properties. This means the Engine can change how it reasons without breaking the confirmed contract.

decisions.context: Implement one thin vertical slice as a self-contained Python module with a deterministic demonstration and a few focused tests.
Add a small deterministic reflection layer that recognizes a few explicit observation signals and changes the next proposal for the relevant active goal, while leaving unrelated goals unchanged.

Add a small end-to-end regression scenario with a controllable model adapter, then validate the resulting proposals against explicit behavioral checks. Keep one separately recorded real-model run for qualitative review.

Refactor the runner so the Engine returns a pending proposal rather than creating a Goal directly. Add an explicit participant decision step that can accept, modify, or reject the proposed goal, and only then update the Case File's goals. Keep the first implementation narrow: support acceptance and rejection, with modification represented as participant-supplied goal data if the existing model allows it.

Add a deterministic end-to-end regression scenario for the correction path. Have the Engine propose an interpretation, apply a participant correction, confirm that no goal is created from the uncorrected interpretation, then run the next step and verify that the proposal reflects the corrected direction while unrelated goals and prior observations remain unchanged.

Add one deterministic persistence regression that pauses the scenario, serializes the Case File, reloads it into a fresh Engine, and continues the interaction. Compare the post-reload result with the uninterrupted path.
Create a deterministic two-goal scenario with at least two observations and a pending interpretation
